Every reader of the spec reads it as one document, whether it is one file or thirty

The spec is about to be stored as a core file plus part files. This is the
infrastructure for that, landed while the spec is still ONE file, so the move
itself changes nothing but bytes on disk.

The core owns the order. `guardrails/specformat.py` gains `parts_map`,
`spec_paths` and `read_document`: a core's `## Parts map` table names its parts
in concatenation order, and nothing else lists them. An empty map — the state
today — means the core IS the whole document, so `read_document` hands back the
file's own bytes and every consumer behaves exactly as before. That identity is
the proof this commit rests on: the seven format gates print byte-identical
lines on the live spec, and the committed index is byte-identical to a fresh
build.

The consumers now take a document, not a path. `tests/conftest.py` `read()` is
the one node ~118 test files read the spec through, and it joins the parts back
into one text. The gates and the builder take a list of paths on the command
line — `check-requirement-shape`, `check-vocabulary`, `check-no-history`,
`check-one-name`, `check-weak-words`, `check-index-generated` (its committed
index stays the LAST argument), `check-size-ratchet`, `scripts/build-index.py`,
and `check-criterion-readability`, an eighth consumer of the same shape whose
recorded baselines would otherwise count the core alone. A path that names a
core expands to that core and its parts, so the hardcoded two-argument call in
`guardrails/pre-push` keeps working; sameness is decided on the resolved file,
so a part named twice in two spellings is still read once.

Freshness (gate a) reads `git log -- PRODUCT_SPEC.md spec/`: a change landing in
a part is no longer invisible to the record it is measured against.

Red before green. `tests/test_spec_parts.py` proves the aggregation over
fixtures now, rather than waiting for the move: a core and two parts index,
parse and read as the one file they were cut from; a part dropped from the map
reds the index gate naming the code it carried (INV-259); a part the map names
and the tree lacks reds by name; and the join's newline is load-bearing — the
part fixture ends without one, and without the join the second requirement stops
parsing. `tests/test_index_generated.py` carries the same missing-part proof
over the live spec, guarded: while the map is empty there is no part to drop and
it says so.

PRODUCT_SPEC.md is untouched. The physical parts-map table does not land here:
`guardrails/doc-bounds.json` allows 703126 bytes against 703125 measured, one
byte of headroom, and the ceiling is not this delivery's to raise. An absent map
and an empty map are the same thing to every reader above, so the tree is whole
without it.

    if RETURN in s:

def spec_name_uses(source, filename):
    """Every place a test module names the spec file, and whether that naming is a READ.

    Returns `[(line, is_read)]` for each `"PRODUCT_SPEC.md"` string constant in the module, read off
    the parsed tree rather than off the text: a substring scan catches the spelling it was written
    against and nothing else, and this rule has to hold for the CLASS — `open(...)`, a pathlib
    `(ROOT / name).read_text()`, a `Path(...).open()`, a name handed to a helper — not for one
    subclass of it.

    A naming is legal when the constant is the SOLE argument of a call to `read` or `read_flat`:
    that is the one node, and it is the only form that returns the whole document once the parts
    map names parts. A docstring or an assertion message may say the name freely — a string that is
    never handed to anything is not a read.
    """
    uses = []
    tree = ast.parse(source, filename)
    reading_calls = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and len(node.args) == 1 and not node.keywords:
            fn = node.func
            name = fn.attr if isinstance(fn, ast.Attribute) else getattr(fn, "id", None)
            if name in ("read", "read_flat"):
                reading_calls.add(id(node.args[0]))
        if isinstance(node, (ast.Expr, ast.Assign)) or isinstance(node, ast.JoinedStr):
            continue
    docstrings = set()
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, (ast.Module, ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
            body = getattr(node, "body", None)
            if body and isinstance(body[0], ast.Expr) and isinstance(body[0].value, ast.Constant) \
                    and isinstance(body[0].value.value, str):
                docstrings.add(id(body[0].value))
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, ast.Constant) and node.value == SPEC:
            if id(node) in docstrings:
                continue
            uses.append((node.lineno, id(node) in reading_calls))
    return uses


class TestTheSuiteHasOneReadingNode(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_no_test_reads_the_spec_off_its_own_path(self):
        """The claim the whole split rests on: the suite reads the spec through ONE node.

        It was not true when that node landed. 49 sites opened
        `os.path.join(ROOT, "PRODUCT_SPEC.md")`, and five more reached the same file by a different
        spelling — `(ROOT / "PRODUCT_SPEC.md").read_text()` — including one module whose own `_read`
        helper shadowed the node's name while bypassing it. Every one of them would have kept
        passing over the CORE ALONE the moment a part existed: green over a fraction of the
        document, which is worse than red.

        So the rule is checked on the parsed tree: wherever a test names the spec file, that name
        must be the sole argument of `read`/`read_flat`. The first version of this guard scanned for
        the substring `open(` on the same line and found four of the five pathlib readers not at
        all — a guard for one spelling is not a guard for the rule.
        """
        offenders = []
        for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "tests", "*.py"))):
            if os.path.basename(path) in ("conftest.py", os.path.basename(__file__)):
                continue        # the node itself, and this guard, name the file by their nature
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                source = f.read()
            for line, is_read in spec_name_uses(source, path):
                if not is_read:
                    offenders.append("%s:%d" % (os.path.basename(path), line))
        self.assertEqual(offenders, [],
                         "a test names the spec file somewhere other than a read()/read_flat() call "
                         "— it reads the file itself and would go blind to every part the map "
                         "names: %s" % ", ".join(offenders))

    def test_the_guard_names_a_reader_that_walks_around_the_node(self):
        """Red proof for the guard above: each spelling a test could reach the file by is caught.

        Without this, the guard's green says only that nothing matched — including the case where
        it matches nothing because it cannot see. The four shapes below are the ones that were
        actually found in this suite, plus the helper-shadow that hid one of them.
        """
        walkarounds = [
            'x = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "PRODUCT_SPEC.md"), encoding="utf-8").read()\n',
            'x = (ROOT / "PRODUCT_SPEC.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8")\n',
            'x = Path("PRODUCT_SPEC.md").open().read()\n',
            'def _read(rel):\n    return (ROOT / rel).read_text()\nx = _read("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")\n',
            'PATHS = ["PRODUCT_SPEC.md"]\nx = open(PATHS[0]).read()\n',
        ]
        for src in walkarounds:
            uses = spec_name_uses(src, "<walkaround>")
            self.assertTrue(uses and not any(is_read for _line, is_read in uses),
                            "the guard passed a reader that walks around the node:\n%s" % src)
        for src in ['x = read("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")\n',
                    'x = read_flat("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")\n',
                    'x = conftest.read("PRODUCT_SPEC.md")\n']:
            uses = spec_name_uses(src, "<node>")
            self.assertTrue(uses and all(is_read for _line, is_read in uses),
                            "the guard named the one node as an offender:\n%s" % src)

work rather than by the next review. Each was a place the rule answered
confidently and wrongly, which is worse than the silences it replaced.

Rebinding by assignment was a set union, so `tracked = read` followed by

added and nothing took it away. The bindings are now walked in source order and

where it stands.

"tests", "fixtures")` — was taken for the root itself, so a fixture document
under it would have been flagged as this one. It is not the root, and the
distinction is the shape: a walk-up ending in a join or a `/` is a descent.

All six shapes are in the guard's proof list now: the two rebinding orders, the
function-local shadow, the fixture descent, plus the alias and REPO_ROOT cases
